stories.title: Plastic sector stocks overview
stories.summary: Plastic stocks represent companies involved in the manufacturing, processing and distribution of plastic-based products. These businesses serve industries including packaging, construction, automobiles, healthcare and agriculture. The sector encompasses a wide range of companies that supply materials for everyday consumer goods and industrial applications.

stories.title: Gujarat leads in compostable plastic manufacturing
stories.summary: Gujarat has emerged as India's largest hub for compostable plastic manufacturing, hosting 62 of the country's nearly 400 certified units. State-wise data from the Central Pollution Control Board shows Gujarat leads Tamil Nadu and Maharashtra in registered production capacity. The state is currently pushing a circular economy agenda.

stories.title: Guwahati municipal body threatens trade licence cancellations
stories.summary: The Guwahati Municipal Corporation has warned shopkeepers that using banned single-use plastic items will result in trade licence cancellations. The corporation says the move is a pragmatic deterrent, though it acknowledges that continued use of plastic carry bags will significantly undermine the city's ban.

stories.title: Plastic waste crisis persists
stories.summary: Plastic waste reflects national consumption and disposal habits. While grocery bags and food containers provide convenience, their disposal harms animals and pollutes waterways. Weak enforcement and a lack of affordable alternatives allow unnecessary plastic use to continue, despite calls for consumers to recycle more effectively.

stories.title: High Court dismisses customs appeal on plastic waste
stories.summary: The Gujarat High Court dismissed a customs appeal regarding the export of gutkha in plastic packaging. The court upheld a tribunal decision that the Plastic Waste Management and Handling Rules of 2011 did not apply to the specific export case, setting aside previous confiscations and penalties.

stories.title: Bengaluru corporation collects fines for plastic violations
stories.summary: The Bengaluru South City Corporation collected Rs 39,800 in fines during a campaign against improper waste management and single-use plastic. Officials have instructed commercial establishments and street vendors to dispose of waste scientifically, following a directive from the Greater Bengaluru Development Minister.

stories.title: Delhi considers deposit return scheme for plastic
stories.summary: The Delhi government is considering a deposit return scheme for plastic bottles and tobacco packaging to encourage recycling. Environment Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa said the plan aims to prevent recyclable waste from harming the environment. Consumers would pay a refundable deposit when purchasing selected products.

stories.title: Delhi weighs deposit refunds for plastic bottles
stories.summary: The Delhi government is evaluating a deposit-return scheme for plastic bottles and tobacco packaging. Under the proposal, consumers would pay a refundable deposit at the point of purchase, which is returned upon bringing empty items to collection points. The government expects this to reduce landfill waste.

stories.title: Plastic Antioxidants Market Segmentation Analysis Reveals High-Growth Opportunities Through 2030 - EIN News
Plastics polymers market forecast to grow
stories.summary: The global plastics polymers market is projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate of 5.6 percent through 2030. The Business Research Company reports that demand is rising across diverse industries, fueled by innovation and increasing application areas for polymer materials.

stories.title: Plastic to fuel market growth projected
stories.summary: The plastic to fuel market is expected to reach 2.67 billion dollars by 2030, growing at a compound annual growth rate of 24.8 percent. The sector is gaining traction as a method to manage plastic waste by transforming refuse into an alternative energy source.

stories.title: ETFE seals market demand rises
stories.summary: The global ETFE seals market is entering 2026 with broader demand from high-tech and industrial sectors. According to an IndexBox report, the market is characterized by chemical resistance and thermal stability, navigating a landscape shaped by supply chain pressures and disciplined procurement behavior.

stories.title: Polymer chips market enters expansion phase
stories.summary: The global polymer chips market is entering a phase of steady expansion, driven by demand from the packaging, automotive and construction sectors. An IndexBox report notes that the market is defined by the dominance of commodity polymers such as polyethylene and polypropylene.

stories.title: Plastic additives market growth driven by packaging
stories.summary: The plastic additives and stabilizers industry is seeing growth driven by rising demand for flexible packaging. The market is expanding as sectors seek improved performance, durability and safety for plastic materials. The industry is currently focused on developing specialized products to meet these evolving requirements.

stories.title: Global Plastic Resin Prices: Supply, Demand and Market Trends - Grand View Research
Polyvinyl Chloride Packaging Film Market Size Report, 2035 - Grand View Research
Renewable chemicals market scales commercially
stories.summary: The global renewable chemicals market is entering a phase of accelerated commercial scaling. Brand owners and chemical producers are aligning capital spending with decarbonization targets. Bio-based polymers are increasingly being qualified for use across the packaging, automotive and consumer goods sectors.

stories.title: Global tensions highlight the need for greater plastic recycling
stories.summary: The Age of Parity is becoming visible in real time as surging fuel costs trigger economic shocks. While the circumstances in Syria remain particular to that country, the larger economic lesson is that energy shocks quickly become economic shocks. Oil prices continue to influence global manufacturing costs.

stories.title: ICC highlights role for smarter design in plastics that escape waste systems
stories.summary: The International Chamber of Commerce is drawing attention to material design for plastic that never reaches formal waste management. The organization is examining technologies aimed at products likely to leak into nature while negotiators work toward a future Global Plastics Treaty. Specialized working bodies are currently involved.

stories.title: Belgium recycled 83% of household packaging waste in 2024
stories.summary: Belgium recycled 83% of its household packaging waste in 2024, up from 79% in 2023. Plastic remains the least recycled category at 58%, while glass reached 98%. The figures were published by Statbel, the Belgian statistical office, to mark the European Week for Waste Reduction.

stories.title: Global Petrochemical Recycling Market Size Forecast To Cross $33.28 Billion By 2030 - EIN News
BPF sets out roadmap to increase EPS recycling to 80% by 2035
stories.summary: The British Plastics Federation aims to increase expanded polystyrene recycling to 80% by 2035, with an interim target of 68% by 2030. The material accounts for less than 1% of UK plastic packaging. It is a single-material product containing around 98% air.

stories.title: Researchers turn hard-to-recycle PVC into high-performance lubricant oil
stories.summary: Researchers at Virginia Tech developed a chemical process to transform PVC into polyalphaolefin, a synthetic base oil used in high-performance lubricants. The findings, published in Nature, suggest a way to repurpose PVC, which is difficult to recycle due to its chlorine content and various additives.

stories.title: Reconomy opens £20m plastic recycling facility in Corby
stories.summary: Reconomy has opened a £20m, 138,000-square-foot plastic recycling facility in Northamptonshire. The plant can process 38,000 tonnes of plastic annually, focusing on packaging collected before it reaches supermarket shelves. The site has created more than 30 long-term local jobs to support a closed-loop system.

stories.title: Enzymes with an appetite for plastic
stories.summary: Biorecycling, or enzymatic recycling, is being positioned as an alternative to mechanical and chemical recycling. Proponents suggest it avoids the heavy machinery and high energy demands associated with traditional chemical recycling methods. The process is currently being explored as a way to tackle plastic waste.

stories.title: Glass packagers welcome updates in modulated pEPR fee approach
stories.summary: Glass packaging groups have welcomed amendments to the modulated Extended Producer Responsibility fee classifications. The changes aim to incentivize materials that are easier to recycle. Compliance schemes noted an overall increase in costs for the industry as the new fee structure takes effect.

stories.title: PackUK publishes confirmed EPR fees for 2026/27
stories.summary: PackUK has confirmed its packaging waste disposal fees for 2026/27. For the first time, producers will pay modulated fees based on recyclability ratings. Green-rated packaging will attract lower fees, while red-rated packaging incurs higher costs. The system aims to incentivize sustainable design through financial penalties and rewards.

stories.title: UK pEPR fees spark mixed industry reactions
stories.summary: PackUK has confirmed its 2026 to 2027 packaging EPR fees, utilizing a traffic light system to reward recyclability. Ecosurety warned that higher-than-expected costs for plastic and wood could undermine producer planning. Meanwhile, British Glass welcomed the modulated fees as an opportunity to strengthen the UK circular economy.

stories.title: Government questioned over transparency of pEPR
stories.summary: Environment Minister Emma Hardy defended the transparency of the packaging Extended Producer Responsibility scheme on 18 November. The response highlighted existing operational plans and producer-led work but offered no new timelines for data disclosure. The exchange followed discrepancies between illustrative and confirmed 2026/27 producer fees.

stories.title: PackUK posts final 2026/27 packaging fees for producers
stories.summary: PackUK has released the final 2026/27 packaging fees under the extended producer responsibility regime. The charges, which apply from April 1, 2026, are available via an online calculator. Harder-to-recycle packaging carries higher costs under the new regulatory framework published on GOV.UK.

stories.title: PackUK EPR fees higher than illustrative estimates
stories.summary: Confirmed 2026/27 packaging EPR fees are higher than the illustrative estimates published in December 2025. Wood and plastic saw the largest increases, rising by £131 and £50 per tonne respectively. This is the first year that fees are modulated based on recyclability under the new methodology.

stories.title: Glass holds steady as British Glass welcomes certainty on pEPR fees
stories.summary: Glass accounts for approximately 94% of green-rated packaging on the UK market, according to recent figures. It currently holds the lowest per-tonne fee of any major packaging material. British Glass expects a meaningful reduction in future fees as the scheme transitions into its third and fourth years.

stories.title: Mandatory EPR obligations in Mexico
stories.summary: Mexico has incorporated extended producer responsibility into its General Law of Circular Economy, requiring manufacturers to finance and organize packaging recovery. Although the law is published, the specific rules required to trigger these legal obligations have not yet been established, nearly a year after the law's debut.

stories.title: PackUK publishes confirmed packaging EPR fees for 2026/27
stories.summary: PackUK has released confirmed fees for large producers, featuring the first modulated rates linked to recyclability. Red-rated materials are set at 1.2 times the amber base rate for 2026/27. Green-rated discounts are determined by the relative proportion of materials reported through the official data service.

stories.title: Amcor to explore fiber-based packaging with FluidSolids partnership
stories.summary: Amcor is partnering with FluidSolids to evaluate fiber-based biocomposites for rigid packaging closures. The collaboration focuses on performance and manufacturability using cellulosic fiber waste and natural binders. These materials are designed to break down under home-composting conditions, offering an alternative end-of-life solution for consumer packaging.

stories.title: AilArian introduces illuminated packaging
stories.summary: AilArian is offering early access to illuminated packaging technology, which uses magnetically recoverable conductive inks to create engaging product presentations. The company plans to establish a circular ecosystem for printed electronics through a take-back system. Packaging can now be designed to bring products to life, literally.

stories.title: AilArian opens early access to sustainable illuminated packaging technology
stories.summary: AilArian is opening early access to its illuminated packaging technology, featuring paper-based circuits and magnetically recoverable conductive inks. The company says it wants to give brands the opportunity to create more engaging experiences while moving the industry toward a circular approach. Production opportunities are open for 2027.

stories.title: Amcor, FluidSolids to test fibre bio-composites for rigid packaging - Packaging Gateway
Amcor and FluidSolids explore compostable rigid packaging
stories.summary: Amcor has partnered with Swiss firm FluidSolids to evaluate fibre-based biocomposites for rigid packaging closures. The platform uses natural binders and cellulosic fibre waste designed to break down under home-composting conditions. The companies are currently focusing on performance, manufacturability and potential scale-up for consumer goods.

stories.title: Smart tag packaging market grows
stories.summary: The smart tag packaging market is expanding as industries demand smarter solutions for product identification and tracking. Growth is driven by technological advancements and the need for transparency across global supply chains. The sector is currently focused on innovations in paper-based NFC technology to shape future packaging trends.

stories.title: Kraft paper honeycomb core market shifts to industrial use
stories.summary: The global kraft paper honeycomb core market is entering a phase of structural expansion through 2035. Demand is shifting from traditional logistics toward higher-value structural and industrial applications. The material, made by expanding kraft paper into a hexagonal cell structure, is noted for its strength-to-weight ratio.

stories.title: VPK Packaging unveils StandIT single-piece packaging format - Packaging Gateway
Recyclable design to shape packaging
stories.summary: Henkel’s Rajat Agarwal told the Brueckner Group Customer Day that inline barrier coatings, material innovation and recyclability testing are key to sustainable packaging. The industry is focusing on these elements to transition toward more recyclable designs over the next decade. Sustainability is now a technical requirement.

stories.title: Nichrome’s NH-150 HFFS machine at PMEC 2026 - Packaging South Asia
Automated shrink wrapping aids liquid shipping
stories.summary: A cleaning brand has invested in a Pratika L Sealer and tunnel to manage increased online sales of liquid products. The equipment features adapted product guides to accommodate cylindrical bottles that standard machines could not handle. The company previously relied on a semi-automatic line for its packaging needs.

stories.title: Doctor blades market demand linked to press utilization
stories.summary: The global doctor blades market is entering 2026 with more disciplined procurement behavior. Demand for these precision components is driven by press utilization, line speeds and maintenance cycles in downstream plants rather than standalone blade consumption. Packaging converters are currently adding flexible barrier and high-graphics capacity.

stories.title: Automatic strip packaging machine market forecast
stories.summary: The global automatic strip packaging machine market is undergoing study to identify growth pathways and leading players through 2032. The sector is characterized by detailed market information, error-free statistics and reliable forecasts. Players are using this data to take advantage of emerging trends and regional expansion opportunities.

stories.title: Top 6 Engineering Advantages to Look for When Choosing a flexible Bag Making Machine Manufacturer - EIN News
Blister packaging machine market transforms
stories.summary: The global blister packaging machines market is entering a decade of transformation as manufacturers reassess automation readiness and regulatory compliance. Demand is closely tied to pharmaceutical and medical device production. The market enters 2026 with broader demand fundamentals and a more regionally diversified supply architecture.

stories.title: Die-cutter market advances with automation
stories.summary: The die-cutter market is projected to expand at a 5.7% CAGR through 2036. Packaging converters are investing in integrated automation, print registration and postpress technologies to manage complex formats. The industry is shifting toward machinery modernization to improve production efficiency and handle increasingly automated packaging workflows.

stories.title: Shrink wrapping provides faster shipping solution
stories.summary: A company has replaced its semi-automatic line with a Pratika L Sealer and tunnel to support growth in online sales. The new equipment uses adapted product guides to wrap unusually shaped cylindrical bottles. The move is intended to ensure products remain aligned for a neat pack every time.

stories.title: Supreme Court directs front-of-package labelling
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has issued directions to the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India regarding front-of-package nutritional warning labels. The order follows proceedings over delays in implementation. Packaged food brands may now face changes in product formulation, packaging design and brand communication across the industry.

stories.title: Supreme Court orders prominent food warnings
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has directed the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India to introduce prominent warnings for packaged foods high in sugar, salt and fat. The order requires products exceeding specific thresholds to carry distinct labels. India's FMCG brands are now preparing for significant communication changes.

stories.title: Greece starts national bottle deposit scheme
stories.summary: Greece has launched a deposit return system for single-use plastic bottles and aluminium cans. Shoppers will pay an extra €0.10 or €0.15 per container at checkout, which is refundable upon return. The system aims to create a complete cycle for recycling packaging back into raw materials.

stories.title: SC tightens food labelling norms, says warning labels must appear separately on front of packaging - Moneycontrol.com
Supreme Court issues directions on front-of-pack warning labels for packaged foods - BMI
Cilicant receives industry awards for pharma support
stories.summary: Cilicant Private Limited has won the India Pharma Award for Excellence in Ancillary and Support Services. The company also received recognition from a global healthcare brand for its role as a trusted partner. These honours highlight the firm's focus on product integrity and shelf life.

stories.title: Supreme Court orders separate warning labels for high salt, sugar and fat on food packs - Telegraph India
Tetra Pak introduces spoonable food carton
stories.summary: Tetra Pak has launched the Tetra Reva, a carton designed for spoonable foods. The package features a full-top opening and a pull-ring mechanism intended to replace foil seals. The company claims the shape provides additional space for branding compared to traditional round pots.

stories.title: Beauty brands adopt pharmaceutical packaging styles
stories.summary: Beauty brands are increasingly using pharmaceutical-inspired packaging to signal efficacy and product protection, according to Euromonitor International. As consumer interest in targeted skin care and longevity grows, brands are highlighting active ingredients and clear benefits to meet demand for science-led products.

stories.title: Subam Papers buys 70 percent stake in Star Boxes
stories.summary: Subam Papers has agreed to acquire a 70 percent equity stake in Star Boxes for ₹19.60 crore. The deal marks the company's entry into finished packaging manufacturing. Star Boxes currently maintains an annual capacity of 24,000 metric tonnes of corrugated boxes. Completion is expected by December 20, 2026.

stories.title: Brookfield to acquire PGP Glass
stories.summary: Brookfield has agreed to acquire PGP Glass from Blackstone for USD 1.7 billion. The transaction involves a significant change in ownership for the glass packaging manufacturer. The announcement appeared alongside advice for first-time home buyers regarding the financial responsibilities of property ownership.

stories.title: This Packaging Firm's Rs 54-Crore IPO Opens On December 1. What Should Investors Know - NDTV
Enjay Converters acquires New Method Packaging
stories.summary: Specialty packaging group Enjay Converters has acquired Ohio-based New Method Packaging. The group is controlled by an investor syndicate led by Champlain Financial Corporation. Financial terms of the acquisition were not disclosed in the announcement.

stories.title: Enjay Converters Ltd ("Enjay"), a leading specialty packaging group controlled by an investor group led by the Champlain
Banks finance KKR acquisition of Logoplaste
stories.summary: Banks have lined up €550 million in loans to support KKR's acquisition of packaging company Logoplaste. The financing package is intended to facilitate the buyout of the firm, which specialises in rigid plastic packaging solutions for the food and beverage industry.

stories.title: SIG begins construction on Ahmedabad carton plant
stories.summary: SIG has laid the foundation for its first aseptic carton plant in Ahmedabad, India. The company is investing approximately INR 525.98 crores to reach an initial capacity of 4 billion packs per year. Plans exist to eventually scale the facility to 10 billion packs annually.

stories.title: Ball Corporation to build beverage can plant in Uttar Pradesh
stories.summary: Ball Corporation will invest USD 300 million to build a two-line aluminium beverage can factory in Meerut. The facility is expected to begin production in 2029 and will serve as the company's third manufacturing site in India. It is located along the Ganga Expressway.
